content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a Hyperbolic Binary Neural Network (HBNN) by representing the parameter vector of Euclidean space in the hyperbolic space, which would make it possible to optimize the parameter in an unconstrained space. By analyzing the parameterized representation, they present that the dynamic exponential map is a diffeomorphism in the Poincare ́ ball. Theoretically, this property will not create extra saddle points or local minima in the Poincare ́ ball, which also explains the good performance of the HBNN. Experiments on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet classification datasets with VGGsmall, ResNet18, and ResNet34 demonstrate the superiorities of HBNN over existing methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
1. The paper is closely relevant to representation learning. 
2. The proposed method achieves good performance. 
3. The proposed method is explained with visualized representation.

Weakness
1. The theoretical contribution of the proposed method is limited. They represent the parameter vector in the Euclidean space as the one in the hyperbolic space so as to optimize the parameter in an unconstrained space. However, most of the theory proof is from the existing work and there is not challenge for them to apply these theories.
2. The results do not support the theory. They assert that “Theoretically, this property will not create extra saddle points or local minima in the Poincare ́ ball” in the abstract. However, in the results of Figure 5 ( c ) in the appendix, I see there are many local minima.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. The clarity needs to be improved. Figure 2 is not informative and kind of confusing, what is the relationship between different subfigures? I suggest the authors move the hyper-parameter study of Table 1 into the appendix and put other important experimental results former.
2. Originality is poor. They exploit many existing theories, and it is more like an applied paper but without certain technical challenges.
content.summary_of_the_review:
This paper proposes a Hyperbolic Binary Neural Network by representing the parameter vector of Euclidean space in the hyperbolic space, which would make it possible to optimize the parameter in an unconstrained space. By analyzing the parameterized representation, they present that the dynamic exponential map is a diffeomorphism in the Poincare ́ ball and assert that this property will not create extra saddle points or local minima in the Poincare ́ ball. Experiments on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet classification datasets demonstrate the superiorities. 

However, there are some weak points, as follows.
1. The theoretical contribution is minor and the technical contribution is not enough compared with existing works. 
This paper applies some existing theories to their solution. However, the technical challenge of applying these theories is not significant.
2. The experimental results are not consistent with the idea. 
They assert that “Theoretically, this property will not create extra saddle points or local minima in the Poincare ́ ball” in the abstract. However, in the visualized results, there are many local minima.
3. The writing and organization need to be polished.
Figure 2 is not informative and kind of confusing about the relationship between different subfigures. The position of experimental results could be rearranged to put the important results in front.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a version of hyperbolic binary neural network, by simply putting the weight into hyperbolic space and then binarize it during the network forward. The rest steps (backward) follow the same manner as regular BNN. Some experiments with minor improvement were shown in the paper.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
It's an interesting idea to explore quantized hyperbolic neural network. However, the paper overall has severe drawbacks with respect to its methodolot. 
1. A binary projection projects a points into a specific set of discrete points in the space. In the hyperbolic space case, it binaries each point into point as ($\pm$1,$\pm$1, ..., $\pm$1) in the Poincare ball, which is still a point in the hyperbolic space. Then, this paper directly regard this point as a Euclidean point, apply Euclidean sign function on these points and use euclidean loss functions, which doesn't make sense at all since all the hyperbolic geometry is lost. The sign function and loss function are not defined for manifolds and the hyperbolic space is not even a vector space. 

2. One main contribution the author claims is the unconstrained optimization in the hyperbolic space, however, It's straightforward and not novel to make a constrained learning over a manifold into an unconstrained one, by simply using the exponential map and optimize in the tangent space. In fact, it's just a simple math trick. 

3. The writing and words need to be polished. The authors are not even confident with what they are doing, e.g., page 2 end of motivation part, "... seems reasonable and helpful", page 2 the 2nd contribution, "which seems to indicate ...", and even for their theorem and proof, page 6, s4.1, the paragraph after theorem 1, ".., it seems that $\phi$ is indeed a diffeomorphism", so it is or it isn't? and there are many other similar sentences and examples in the paper. The proofs (3 of them) are even ridiculous, just one sentence, "Proof. The proofs can be found in ..." .... 

4. Very limited related work, the improvement are nearly none, and no variance results are given...
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Low quality, many theoretical and empirical claims are not well supported, not original.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a binarization of neural network based on a hyperbolic mapping between the constrained optimization of the loss function and its unconstrained counterpart on the Poincare disc.   After a brief introduction of basic concepts in differential geometry, the authors present the results of their algorithm on CFRA-10 and ImageNet using standard architectures ResNet-18, ResNet-34 and VGG-Small. Their results show noteworthy improvement over state of the art.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths

o A novel method based on non-Euclidean geometry is leveraged competently
o An algorithm is developed and outlined 
o Computational results are reported that exceed state of the art

Weaknesses

o Explanation as to why the authors use this method is obscure
o The preliminaries section is quite vague and at times inaccurate (see below)
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The idea of optimization in non-Euclidean space with negative curvature is not new and the authors use it deftly without being able to convince the reader why.  The obscure analogy used in the last sentence in first paragraph of Motivation or the sentence starting with "As for the reason why hyperbolic ..." in the paragraph with sub-heading HBNN vs Mirror Descent in Sec 4.2 on page 6 are not helpful.  The authors also are unclear what the terms constrained or unconstrained exactly refer to.  Is it optimization over the discrete set {-1,+1}^n the constrain they refer to or is it the range of 'w' and 'a' values imposed in the Euclidean space?  What is the role of 'r' in the Poincare disc?  Is it the curvature, used in numerical results for D_1 and D_0.05?   Judging the paper by the Tables 2 and 3, it clearly makes a contribution since he reported state of the art is exceeded.  But significant vagueness exists in multiple parts of the text, from abstract up to Section 4.2 when experimental results are reported.  To wit:

- (Abstract): By analyzing the parameterized representation, we present that the dynamic exponential map is a diffeomorphism in the Poincare ball. Theoretically, this property will not create extra saddle points or local minima in the Poincare ball.  
<-- What does a diffeomorphism got to do with existence of local/global minima?  One can smoothly bend a straight-line (no minima) to create one or more local minima or a global minimum

- Specifically, we propose a Hyperbolic Binary Neural Network (HBNN) that represents the parameter vector in the Euclidean space as the one in the hyperbolic space
<-- As a parameter vector in hyperbolic space?  If so does just mean we map a point in E^n to H^n?

- Theoretically, the dynamic exponential map is a diffeomorphism in the Poincare ball, and will not add extra saddle points or local minima, which seems to indicate that ...
<-- Seems to whom?

- For an n-dimensional connected manifold M, the tangent space at a point p in M is defined as TpM.
<-- Do we mean an n-dimensional connected differentiable manifold?

- this unconstrained problem is the multi-objective optimization
<-- What are the multiplicities of the objectives here?

The authors also miss a recent result for  CFAR-10. The binary AdaBin (ResNet-18) gives accuracy 93.1.

One page 1, the authors mean {-1,+1} and not (-1,+1).
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper has strong enough results to justify a definite acceptance.  But the writing and the above-mentioned vagueness are an impediment to a strong recommendation.  A more clearly-written paper with crisper explanations up to Section 4.2 would be a much stronger paper assuming the results are valid.  Without publicly available code it is hard to say so definitely.

content.title: Hyperbolic Binary Neural Network
content.TL;DR: We propose a Hyperbolic Binary Neural Network that updates the parameters in hyperbolic space.
content.abstract: Binary Neural Network (BNN) converts the full-precision weights and activations to the extreme 1-bit counterparts, which is especially suitable to be deployed on lightweight mobile devices. Neural network binarization is usually formulated as a constrained optimization problem, which restricts its optimized potential. In this paper, we introduce the dynamic exponential map that converts a constrained problem in the Riemannian manifold into an unconstrained one in the Euclidean space. Specifically, we propose a Hyperbolic Binary Neural Network (HBNN) by representing the parameter vector in the Euclidean space as the one in the hyperbolic space, which would enable us to optimize the parameter in an unconstrained space. By analyzing the parameterized representation, we present that the dynamic exponential map is a diffeomorphism in the Poincaré ball. Theoretically, this property will not create extra saddle points or local minima in the Poincaré ball, which also explains the good performance of the HBNN. Experiments on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet classification datasets with VGGsmall, ResNet18, and ResNet34 demonstrate the superiorities of our HBNN over existing state-of-the-art methods.
